NOTES:
1. Ordering approval includes approval of all commercial terms and conditions settled with the supplier. However:
(a) Financial Concurrence is required for payment of advance including activity linked payment (drawing/ engg. documentation etc.) in stages.
(b) Unsecured advance to foreign suppliers upto a maximum of US$ 20,000 (or equivalent) may be granted with financial concurrence of HOF and approval of Unit Head in exceptional circumstances which must be placed on record.
(c) Approval of the Unit Head is required for waiver of Bank Guarantee towards advance to PSUs/ Govt. departments or towards safe custody and return of equipment after repairs etc./ material after processing/ conversion/ machining etc. Reasons/ circumstances warranting waiver of BG under exceptional circumstances shall be recorded and suitable coverage under insurance policy shall be ensured.
(d) Unit Head is empowered to accord approval for interest bearing secured advance in case of R&D items which are non-repetitive and below a tender estimate value of Rs. 20 Lakhs. Such advance payments should not exceed the following limits:
(i) 40% of contract value to a State or Central Government agency or PSUs
(ii) 30% of contract value to private firms
In all other cases, Unit Head is empowered only upto 5% of PO value.
(Note: Interest rate shall be the repo rate (on the date of release of advance) plus 4% which shall be indicated in the NIT. The interest rate shall be valid during the currency of the contract. Interest rate shall be communicated on an annual basis, by Corporate Finance by 1st of April every year)
2. Where one purchase enquiry is split into more than one ordering proposal, each proposal shall carry the cumulative value of all the proposals and financial concurrence and approving authority shall be based on the cumulative value.
3. For Price escalation claims above the limits in SI. 11 beyond 10% (or Rs 1 Cr/ 5 Cr as applicable) and upto 25% of the contract value, shall require concurrence of Director (Finance) and approval of CMD, provided such escalation claims are reimbursed by Customer on back to back basis.
4. Sanction of extra items etc. as per Sl. 12 beyond 10% of order value (or Rs 1 Cr) shall require concurrence of Director (Finance) and approval of CMD.
5. All cases of waiver of liquidated damages due from suppliers of more than Rs 5 lakh will require concurrence of Director (Finance) and approval of CMD. The proposal of Business Groups to be routed through business group chief.
6. For purchases through Personal Enquiry abroad by overseas sites/ offices, including purchases for project completion items, the financial limits for ED/ GGMs/ GM-I shall be US $ 5,000 for purchases made abroad for foreign site/s against SI No. 16 of DoP. The Unit Heads may sub-delegate their powers to suitable levels of executives as appropriate for smooth operations at overseas sites/ offices and availability of officers at those locations.
7. EDs/ GGMs/ GM-I/ GMs posted in Corporate Office will exercise the same powers as delegated to EDs/ GGMs/ GM-I/ GMs holding the charge of Units.
8. All ex-gratia payments to suppliers with recorded reasons and rationale will require concurrence of Director (Finance) and approval of CMD. The proposal of Business Groups to be routed through Business Group Chief. Such ex-gratia payment can be allowed on back-to-back basis provided BHEL has received a similar payment from the customer.
9. The delegation will hold good in respect of sub-contracting jobs involving use of sub-contractor's material. When the material is issued by BHEL, the powers detailed above will be exercised to the extent of 50% indicated against various cases.
10. Approval taken from higher authority than DoP if required under specific provisions of the Purchase Policy, shall not be construed as exercising the DoP for Inviting Tenders/ Ordering etc.
11. Wherever the price reasonability certified is more than 20% of the estimate, such cases would require approval of authority one step higher than the order approving authority, limited to Unit Head. Further, in such case the written communication of commensurate level (equivalent to the authority empowered for ordering) in PMG of the concerned Business Sector has to be taken on the need for the procurement (as per the project schedule) before ordering.
In cases where Unit Head is empowered to order as per DoP, the Unit Head may constitute a committee of GMs to examine cases wherever the price reasonability certified is more than 20% of the estimate, and then take a decision accordingly.
12. The monthly reports of all cases of ordering at prices at 20 % more than estimate shall be submitted to Head/COC, Corporate Office.
13. For project sites notified by PMG of Business Sector (based on the approval of Functional Director, or CMD in case of Units reporting directly to CMD) the DoP under Clause 16 of DoP (Purchase through Personal Enquiry) is enhanced to twice the existing powers.
14. Any DoP which is beyond the powers delegated upto CMD would require approval of the Board.
